key_insight: Splat2Act shows that a generalist manipulation policy can be personalized to a specific home or office by automatically turning captured scenes into simulation and adapting the policy there first. This closes the gap between strong generic robots and the real-world objects and layouts found in individual users’ environments.
problem_solved: Generalist vision-language-action policies often fail in new, user-specific environments because they have not seen those exact scenes, objects, and placements before. Collecting real demonstrations for every new home or office is too costly and impractical.
method: Capture the target environment and reconstruct it into a simulator using the recorded scene data.
Adapt a pretrained VLA manipulation policy in simulation so it becomes personalized to the user’s layout and objects.
Transfer the adapted policy back to the real environment, reducing the need for new real-world demonstrations.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a practical path to deploy manipulation robots in personalized settings without extensive manual data collection. It suggests a scalable real-to-sim-to-real workflow for adapting foundation policies to many different homes and offices.

paper_title: Splat2Act: From Captured Scenes to Personalized VLA Manipulation
paper_authors: Xiaomeng Ye, Krishna Jaganathan, Gyubeum Lim, Gunjan Chhablani, Muhammad Zubair Irshad
